title: Not Yet Decided
logline: A household has been going back and forth for months over whether one of them should go abroad for work, and nobody in the house can say what has actually been decided.
human_question: When a decision keeps not getting made, what does the waiting itself do to a family?

situation.what_happens: A family is living inside a decision that has not been made. It is not being avoided: there are agency visits, forms begun, documents gathered, medicals discussed, and a sum of money that would have to be borrowed before anything could start. Each step is taken and then not followed by the next one. Meanwhile ordinary life carries on at full volume around it, and the undecided thing sits in the middle of the house being referred to obliquely. Much of the year is spent at counters, holding numbers, waiting for offices to confirm things that could be reversed a week later, which is its own kind of not deciding (folded in from IDEA-0044).
situation.who_is_involved: The person who would go, whose reasons change depending on who is asking; the partner or parent who would stay and run everything alone; children who understand more than they are told; older relatives with a firm view; the agency staff who need an answer and a fee; and neighbours whose households already went one way or the other and who are treated as evidence.
situation.what_is_at_stake: Years of a family's life and a large debt taken on in advance of any earnings. On the other side, a household that stays together and stays where it is financially. For the person who would go, the question of whether the version of the family they come back to will be the one they left. For the film, never becoming a pressure on the decision, and never suggesting that a hard choice is a failing.
situation.how_it_unfolds: It begins with a reason that is real, usually a debt or a cost that cannot be met from here. The pressures are an agency's timetable, a document that expires, a relative's opinion, and the slow cost of staying in the same position. It can end with a departure, with a decision not to go, with the question being deferred for another year, or with the choice being taken out of the family's hands by a deadline or a rejection. Reality decides entirely, and the film has to be able to end unresolved, because that is a likely and honest outcome.

concept_merge.why_together: C028 supplies a very precise description of a mind that cannot land: the doubting state is the sparest on the sources' whole list, lacking decision and the desire to act, and the restless state that sits beside it also lacks the desire to act, so neither drives towards anything at all [C028-P:L33; C028-M:L29–L31]. C022 supplies the boundary that makes the film usable: both sources say plainly that ordinary uncertainty about unknown matters is not the unwholesome doubt they mean, which concerns the teacher and the teaching specifically [C022-P:L179; C022-M:L57], and it supplies the source's own image for that doubt, someone arriving at a crossroads for the first time and worn out by not knowing which road to take [C022-P:L179]. The concepts are put together here as a description and its disclaimer, and the disclaimer is half the point.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the texture the sources describe and the texture of a real, honest, unresolved family decision look the same from outside and are not the same thing. Put together, the two concepts let the film say something a viewer can use, that a mind circling without landing is exhausting in a specific way, while refusing the judgement that would normally come attached to it. It also carries the group's handover: after the heat, what is left is not calm but a fog, and the sources are careful to say the fog is not a fault.

concept_links.why: The doubting mind is the sparest of the twelve: it lacks decision (adhimokkha), it lacks the desire to act (chanda), and it has no joy, so it simply circles [C028-P:L33]. Margaya lists the same exclusions [C028-M:L29–L31], and the digest adds that the restless mind beside it also lacks the desire to act, so neither of them drives at anything. That is offered here strictly as an analogy for the lived texture of a long, unresolved decision. The digest puts the matter beyond doubt: 'indecision is a sin' is not the teaching, and the doubt counted in these lists is the unwholesome doubt of Concept 22, about the teacher and the teaching, not ordinary indecision about life choices. The film says that, and never equates the two. The same digest also warns that factor counts are not a severity score and that no fixed recipe of factors may be quoted for any real person's state, which rules out any narration that inventories what is present in this household.

Both sources state that ordinary uncertainty about unknown or undecided matters is not the unwholesome doubt they describe, which is specifically about the teacher and the teaching [C022-P:L179; C022-M:L57]. This film sits entirely inside that ordinary kind, so the concept is linked as a boundary to respect rather than a label to apply, and the digest's 'questioning is a vice' bar is the reading it exists to prevent. Pradeepika's own image for the doubt it does mean is someone reaching a crossroads for the first time, worn out by not knowing which way to go [C022-P:L179], which the film may use for its picture of exhaustion without importing the classification that comes with it. Folded in from IDEA-0044: restlessness, one of the four present in every unwholesome moment [C022-P:L31], is the register of the waiting rooms and counters this decision is largely made of. One limit is technical: the digest notes that L179 mentions eight objects of doubt without listing them, so the film cannot state what they are.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: A choice that keeps circling without landing wears down a whole household, and the texts describe a mind that cannot settle very precisely: no decision in it, no push towards anything, no pleasure either. They are also plain that ordinary uncertainty about an unknown future is not the doubt they warn about, which is about the teaching. So the tiredness is real and it is not a fault.
what_must_be_real: The decision, its timeline and the family's circumstances must be entirely their own and genuinely unresolved when filming begins. No deadline, appointment or conversation may be arranged, and nothing the film does may push the household towards either answer or make either answer harder. Every member shown consents, including the children's guardians, and anyone may stop. The film must be able to end with nothing decided.
position_hint: closing candidate: the group's arc ends in a fog rather than in calm, and a household that genuinely cannot settle a real decision is the most direct human form of that, handing on to the next stage's question of which way to go. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Exploiting real economic hardship for drama, or letting a family's debt become the film's tension.
Implying an honest, difficult life decision is a moral failing, or that the sources' doubt is what this household has.
The story may not resolve within the filming window, which the film must hold as its own true ending rather than manufacturing one.
Becoming a participant in the decision: a camera present at every agency visit is a pressure of its own.
Narrating an inventory of mental factors over a real family, which the digest rules out in as many words.
Children being shown understanding more than the adults have told them.
drop_if: No family in a genuinely unresolved position is willing to be filmed.
The family reaches a firm decision before filming can begin, removing the open question at the centre of the film.
Filming would measurably affect what the family decides.

connections.note: Takes in the counters, the numbers and the half-finished paperwork, which turn out to be what a long decision is actually made of.
Two endings for the group: heat that has already cooled, and a fog that has not lifted.
The heaviness of a task some were urged into, and the deeper stall of a decision nobody can make at all.

selection.reason: Carries EPD-0027 and the group's handover; the merge gives it the waiting rooms that a deferred decision is actually spent in, and a grounded restlessness strand beside the doubt analogy.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
